title: Enterprise-grade features skipped by the minimum-viable autonomy plan: trigger thresholds, solutions, and effort estimates

tldr.content: The minimum-viable-autonomy plan covers 9 controls for single-operator local autonomy and defers 19 enterprise-scale items. The deferral is sound: every skipped item protects against a party or failure mode that does not exist when one operator runs read-only skills on one host. The 19 items become necessary at six threshold events: second operator, second machine, team, external customer, regulatory oversight, or production traffic. Total enterprise build-out: roughly 9-18 engineer-months self-hosted, 4-8 with managed/keyless alternatives.

executiveSummary.content: The 19 skipped items decompose into six clusters mapping to six threshold events. PKI and attestation items (E1-E4) trigger at the second operator or machine. Host hardening items (E5-E8) trigger when the agent handles credentials or runs untrusted generated code. Independent review items (E9-E11) trigger at autonomous writes or compliance requirements. Observability items (E12-E14) trigger at team scale or unattended runs. Evaluation and rollout items (E15-E17) trigger before external users. Continuity items (E18-E19) trigger with shared or customer data. The cheapest upgrade paths are Sigstore keyless signing for E1-E4, OpenTelemetry Collector for E12-E13, and Merkle hash-chaining per RFC 6962 for E14.

keyFindings.content: K1. supported: Deferral is consistent with agentic-security guidance and SRE practice [R1][R2]. K2. supported: Each item solves a structurally absent problem at n=1 [R1][R3]. K3. supported: Single-process role fusion is permitted by RATS architecture [R3]. K4. partially-supported: Six threshold events map to items [R2][R4]. K5. partially-supported: Cheapest upgrades are keyless/managed [R5][R4]. K6. partially-supported: Effort is 9-18 self-hosted / 4-8 managed engineer-months [R5].

detailSections.content:
E1 Key-management service: KMS for key generation/rotation/revocation per NIST SP 800-57. Skip at n=1: OS user boundary is trust anchor. Trigger: second operator/machine. Solution: HashiCorp Vault Transit or Sigstore keyless. Risk: shared static keys, no revocation. Effort: 2-6 weeks KMS / 1-2 weeks keyless.

E2 Signing service: Attestation signing per SLSA v1.2. Skip at n=1: artifacts never leave trust boundary. Trigger: artifacts consumed by others. Solution: cosign signing. Risk: forged provenance. Effort: 2-4 weeks.

E3 Verification service: RATS Verifier role per RFC 9334. Skip at n=1: producer equals consumer. Trigger: second machine consumes. Solution: cosign verify / RATS verifier. Risk: tampered artifacts accepted. Effort: 2-4 weeks.

E4 Signed approvals: OAuth BCP patterns per RFC 9700 (nonce, audience, sender-constraining). Skip at n=1: no token crosses boundary. Trigger: remote approver/daemon. Solution: JWT with iss/aud/jti/nonce/short-exp. Risk: approval replay. Effort: 3 days-2 weeks.

E5 Host daemon mTLS: Per RFC 9700 Section 2.5 recommendation. Skip at n=1: single process. Trigger: second operator/remote. Solution: localhost TLS daemon or Unix socket SO_PEERCRED. Risk: unauthenticated escalation. Effort: 2-4 weeks.

E6 OS-level sink reauthorization: seccomp/systemd per OWASP agentic guidance. Skip at n=1: app-level gates + user account boundary sufficient. Trigger: credentials/shared state. Solution: dedicated OS user + systemd hardening. Risk: prompt injection bypassing app gates. Effort: 1-3 weeks.

E7 Browser isolation: Container-level Chromium per site-isolation principles. Skip at n=1: read-only public web research. Trigger: agent handles valuable sessions. Solution: per-run containerized browser. Risk: session theft. Effort: 1-2 weeks.

E8 Evaluator sandbox: Rootless Docker or bubblewrap. Skip at n=1: generated code stays human-gated. Trigger: autonomous generated-code execution. Solution: rootless Docker with no network. Risk: arbitrary code execution on host. Effort: 1-2 weeks.

E9 Reviewer service: Separate process with own key per separation-of-duties. Skip at n=1: human reviewer is structurally different. Trigger: autonomous writes. Solution: reviewer service with distinct credential. Risk: self-review fraud. Effort: 2-4 weeks.

E10 External validator registry: Versioned attested validator service. Skip at n=1: in-repo digest-pinned validators. Trigger: shared validators/no-redeploy updates. Solution: signed validator bundles. Risk: silent validator substitution. Effort: 2-4 weeks.

E11 Independence verification: Machine-checkable process/credential separation. Skip at n=1: independence is structural. Trigger: both producer and reviewer are software. Solution: KMS-enforced key separation. Risk: collusion undetected. Effort: 1-2 weeks.

E12 OTel Collector: Vendor-agnostic telemetry pipeline. Skip at n=1: local JSONL sufficient. Trigger: second host/alerting/retention. Solution: OTel Collector sidecar/gateway. Risk: no cross-run correlation. Effort: 2-5 days per service.

E13 Metrics/alerting: Prometheus/Grafana with SLO-style alerts per Google SRE. Skip at n=1: operator observes directly. Trigger: unattended/overnight autonomy. Solution: Prometheus + Alertmanager + Grafana. Risk: silent failures discovered late. Effort: 2-4 weeks.

E14 Hash-chained audit: Merkle tree append-only log per RFC 6962 / Rekor. Skip at n=1: git + SQLite is system of record. Trigger: disputes/compliance. Solution: hash-chained records or Rekor. Risk: repudiation, history rewrite. Effort: 3 days-2 weeks.

E15 100+ scenario corpus: Fixed versioned evaluation gate per NIST AI RMF. Skip at n=1: unit + e2e tests cover bounded scope. Trigger: widening autonomy/external users. Solution: versioned corpus in CI. Risk: gate regressions ship silently. Effort: 4-8 weeks initial.

E16 Blinded kappa adjudication: Cohen's kappa per McHugh 2012 (k < 0.60 = inadequate). Skip at n=1: no second rater. Trigger: quality-match claims. Solution: blinded paired adjudication 2+ raters. Risk: self-serving evaluation bias. Effort: 1-2 weeks per round.

E17 Production canary: Partial time-limited deployment vs concurrent control per Google SRE. Skip at n=1: no production traffic. Trigger: serving other users. Solution: traffic-split canary with automated rollback. Risk: version defect reaches whole fleet. Effort: 2-4 weeks.

E18 Privacy review: Per NIST Privacy Framework. Skip at n=1: secrets stripped, local 0600 telemetry. Trigger: telemetry leaves machine/shared data. Solution: DPIA-style review per data flow. Risk: secrets in shared artifacts. Effort: 2-5 days per cycle.

E19 DR with RPO/RTO: Tested snapshot/restore per etcd pattern. Skip at n=1 (minimum form): plan already includes VACUUM INTO backup + verify. Trigger: second machine/HA requirement. Solution: scheduled snapshots + offsite + restore drills. Risk: unrestorable backups. Effort: 1-2 days local / 2-4 weeks enterprise.

recommendation.content: Proceed with the minimum-viable plan unchanged. Treat the six threshold events as the un-skipping checklist. When thresholds are crossed, prefer keyless/managed paths (Sigstore, OTel Collector, Rekor-style chaining) over private PKI. Sequence: trust-boundary items E1-E5 at second operator/machine; host hardening E6-E8 when credentials appear; observability E12-E14 at team scale; evaluation E15-E17 before external users; continuity E18-E19 with shared data.

unverifiedClaims.content: Effort estimates are planning heuristics, not measured schedules. NIST SP 800-57, Privacy Framework, Vault, Prometheus, and bubblewrap were cited at locator level without direct page retrieval. The trigger-to-item mapping is analytical, not normative. RFC 6962 is obsoleted by RFC 9162 for wire formats. OWASP Agentic Top 10 and NIST AI RMF are moving documents.

processAppendix.content: Read-only research against the minimum-viable-autonomy plan. Primary-led with inline challenge and verify. Sources retrieved 2026-08-28. No files created or modified during research. This finding documents the enterprise gap so the minimum-viable plan's deferral decisions are traceable.

claims.statement: The deferral of all 19 enterprise items is consistent with current agentic-security guidance and SRE practice.
Fusing attester, verifier, and relying-party roles into one process is architecturally valid at n=1 per the RATS architecture.
The necessity of the 19 items is governed by six threshold events.
The cheapest enterprise upgrade for E1-E4 is Sigstore keyless signing.
The plan's VACUUM INTO backup plus verify script is a legitimate n=1 seed of E19 disaster recovery.
